name: HigherLowsIntoResistancePrecedeBreakout
quote: If buyers are able to hold the market higher on successive declines, a pattern of higher pivot lows pressing against the resistance area will result. This suggests real buying conviction supporting the move and the potential breakout.
description: Context filter that precedes the best breakouts: a run of successive pivot lows (G01-01) each higher than the last, occurring while price presses against a stable resistance level (recent range high). Mirrored: a run of successive lower pivot highs pressing against a support floor precedes the best downside breakouts.
pseudocode: pivotLow[k] > pivotLow[k+1] for k = 0..(numHigherLows-1) AND highest(high, rangeLookback) is roughly flat over that span

complexity.reason: needs pivot detection plus counting a rising sequence of pivot lows and a check that the resistance ceiling is stable

notes: Same figure/example recurs in Chapter 2's 'Support or Resistance Breaking' trade description (page 61) -- the dedup pass should merge with that chapter's version of this candidate.

name: MultipleInsideBarsContractionBreakout
quote: A series of multiple inside bars on one time frame usually contains a triangle on the lower time frame... they can set up good breakouts with expectations for strong, extended moves away from the pattern.
description: N consecutive inside bars (G01-06), read as a volatility-contraction 'triangle' that favors a directional breakout away from the range once it resolves; a context filter for the breakout entry, not itself an entry.
pseudocode: count(isInsideBar, lag=0..(consecutiveInsideBars-1)) == consecutiveInsideBars

complexity.reason: a fixed-length window loop counting a per-bar condition

notes: Grimes: 'Trading within triangles is usually a losing proposition... but they can set up good breakouts' -- i.e. this is a filter for a subsequent breakout entry, not a standalone entry signal.

name: HigherLowsIntoResistancePrecedeBreakoutTrade
quote: The best resistance breaking trades will be driven by large-scale buying imbalances, and these imbalances usually show, for instance, as the market holds higher lows into the resistance level before the actual breakout.
description: Context filter for the support/resistance-breaking (breakout) trade category: a run of successive higher pivot lows pressing against a stable resistance ceiling precedes the best breakouts. Mirrored for lower highs pressing into a support floor before a breakdown.
pseudocode: pivotLow[k] > pivotLow[k+1] for k = 0..(numHigherLows-1) AND highest(high, rangeLookback) is roughly flat over that span

complexity.reason: needs pivot detection plus counting a rising sequence of pivot lows and a check that the resistance ceiling is stable

notes: Same underlying pattern as G01-05 (Chapter 1's Figure 1.10 preview of this idea); the dedup pass should merge the two -- this file's version ties it explicitly to the support/resistance-breaking trade category, which Chapter 1 only previewed.
chapter_title: The Market Cycle and the Four Trades

name: CleanLevelBreakFollowThrough
quote: Clean levels actually tend to set up good breakout trades beyond the level
description: A level that has shown 1-3 clean price-rejections (G04-02) and is then decisively closed through -- expect strong breakout follow-through; bias entries in the breakout direction rather than fading.
pseudocode: cleanRejectionCount(level, testLookback) >= 1 AND cleanRejectionCount(level, testLookback) <= 3 AND close[0] beyond level by breakMargin*atr(atrLength)
book_order_type: market at next open once broken, per convention

complexity.reason: needs a persistent count of clean-rejection touches against G04-01's level

name: RangeExpansionNotBreakout
quote: Drop below range just expands the range. Support is now lower ... Many times, the range is simply expanded
description: A close beyond the established range boundary that, within M bars, settles back into a new (shifted) but still-bounded range rather than trending away -- treat as range expansion, not a true breakout; do not read the boundary break alone as a trend signal.
pseudocode: close[k] beyond old range boundary for some k in last expandLookback bars AND (highest(high,reboundBars) - lowest(low,reboundBars)) < rangeAtrMultiple*atr(atrLength)

complexity.reason: needs to track the old range boundary through the break and re-test containment afterward

name: DoNotFadeFirstBreakoutFromConvergence
quote: My trading rules for triangles are simple and reduce to one principle: do not fade the first breakout from one of these formations
description: After G04-14 (volatility compression) fires, block countertrend/fade entries on the first close beyond the compressed range's boundary; only with-breakout entries are allowed.
pseudocode: G04-14 fired within compressLookback bars AND proposedEntry direction == breakout direction

complexity.reason: a persistent bars-since flag on G04-14 plus a direction check

name: BarRangeExpansionAtBreakout
quote: we need to see increased volume, activity, and interest associated with the actual breakout... the quantitative measures that will be most useful will be instantaneous measures of volatility such as the ratio of the current bar's range to a window of previous bars.
description: The breakout bar's range (high-low) exceeds a multiple of the average range of the preceding N bars -- confirms a volatile, well-supported breakout.
pseudocode: (high[0] - low[0]) > rangeMultiple * average(high[1..lookback] - low[1..lookback])

complexity.reason: window average of bar range

name: BreakoutVolumeAboveAverage
quote: we need to see increased volume, activity, and interest associated with the actual breakout.
description: Volume on the breakout bar exceeds a multiple of its own N-bar average volume.
pseudocode: volume[0] > volMultiple * average(volume, lookback)

complexity.reason: window average of volume

name: LowerTimeFrameBreakoutEntryApprox
quote: This trade setup times the entry into the pullback by using the momentum of a lower time frame breakout so that the trade will be entered when the market is moving in the intended direction of the trade.
description: Enter the pullback on a breakout of a short-lookback high/low, approximating a lower-time-frame breakout with a much shorter window on the same (trading-time-frame) bars.
pseudocode: close[0] > highest(high[1], ltfLookback)
book_order_type: stop entry on the lower-time-frame breakout -> close-and-next-open

complexity.reason: a short Highest/Lowest window standing in for a genuinely lower time frame

notes: Higher/lower-time-frame reasoning approximated per the mining brief: a 3-bar breakout on the trading time frame stands in for a breakout on a several-times-faster chart. No exact ratio given by the book.

name: BreakoutBaseTightRangeNearResistance
quote: One common form of this pattern is a tight range near the top of a larger range... This small range near a resistance level, usually inside of a larger range, is referred to as a breakout base.
description: A short recent window's height is small relative to a longer window's height, and sits near the top (long) / bottom (short) of that longer window -- the named 'breakout base'.
pseudocode: tightHigh = highest(high, tightLookback); tightLow = lowest(low, tightLookback); rangeHigh = highest(high, rangeLookback); rangeLow = lowest(low, rangeLookback); (tightHigh - tightLow) < tightFraction * (rangeHigh - rangeLow) AND (rangeHigh - tightHigh) < proximityFraction * (rangeHigh - rangeLow)

complexity.reason: two window highest/lowest comparisons, no pivots

notes: Same mechanics as Chapter 5's TightRangeNearLargerRangeExtreme and G06-08; the book names this specific instance 'breakout base'.

name: PriorPenetrationsWeakenBreakout
quote: penetrations of levels before the breakout usually seem to expend some of the energy behind the breakout, and often lead to poor trades.
description: No significant excursion beyond the breakout level occurred in the lookback window before the breakout bar (small failure-test-style probes are fine; a sustained penetration is not).
pseudocode: NOT (any bar in the last preLookback bars closed beyond level by more than a small tolerance for more than maxPriorBarsBeyond consecutive bars)

complexity.reason: a bounded persistent counter over a lookback window

name: BidNearBottomOfBaseEntry
quote: Once the base establishes itself, bid near the bottom of the smaller range.
description: Breakout-base entry trigger 1: enter (limit) near the low of the base's own recent range.
pseudocode: low[0] <= lowest(low[1], baseLookback) + touchTolerance * atr(atrLookback)
book_order_type: limit entry near the base low -> mechanized as close-and-next-open once the bar touches the level

complexity.reason: same mechanics as G06-04

name: EnterAnywhereInBaseSimplified
quote: Just get the position on, anywhere in the range.
description: Breakout-base entry trigger 3: once the base (G06-42) has established itself, enter at the next bar's open without waiting for a bottom-of-base or spring trigger.
pseudocode: BreakoutBaseTightRangeNearResistance -> enter at next open
book_order_type: market entry at the next bar's open

complexity.reason: a direct entry once the base condition is true

name: BreakoutEnterInBaseTemplate
quote: We will first look at some characteristic patterns preceding good breakouts in which the market tips its hand and shows that energy is being built up to support the breakout.
description: The book's named Breakouts, Entering in the Preceding Base template: setup (level tested multiple clean times G06-41, tight base near resistance G06-42 or higher-lows-into-resistance G06-43, no significant prior penetration G06-44) + trigger (bid near base bottom G06-45, spring entry G06-46, or enter-anywhere G06-47) + stop (initial G06-48, tightened on consolidation G06-49) + target (base-width MMO, G06-50).
book_order_type: mixed: G06-45 and G06-46 are limit/stop entries, G06-47 is a market entry

complexity.reason: aggregates hard leg/level-counting setup conditions

notes: Trade type: support/resistance breaking (anticipatory entry). This is functionally a support-holding trade taken before the actual breakout.

name: BreakoutConfirmedByActivityBeyondLevel
quote: The market has made a successful breakout of an important level. Furthermore, there is good activity (volume, volatility, and price action) beyond the level, proving that it was a valid breakout.
description: Setup for the Breakout, First Pullback Following template: the breakout bar shows above-average range and above-average volume (reuses Chapter 5's breakout-quality mechanics).
pseudocode: (high[0] - low[0]) > rangeMultiple * average(high[1..lookback] - low[1..lookback]) AND volume[0] > volMultiple * average(volume, lookback)

complexity.reason: two window averages

name: BreakoutWeakMomentumSetup
quote: Good breakouts should have strong momentum, volume, and interest beyond the level. If this does not happen, it is more likely that the breakout will fail.
description: Warning flag for the Failed Breakouts template: the breakout bar does NOT show above-average range/volume (negation of G06-52) -- raises the odds of failure.
pseudocode: NOT ((high[0] - low[0]) > rangeMultiple * average(high[1..lookback] - low[1..lookback]) AND volume[0] > volMultiple * average(volume, lookback))

complexity.reason: negation of G06-52's two window averages

name: StrongFirstReactionSignalsBreakoutFailure
quote: If the first reaction is very strong (i.e., the first downswing after an upside breakout or vice versa for a breakdown through support), it suggests a failure of the break interest and greatly increased probability of trade failure.
description: The first pullback reaction after a breakout moves with strong momentum against the breakout direction (large body relative to recent average range) -- the trigger for treating the breakout as failing.
pseudocode: close[0] < close[1] AND (open[0] - close[0]) > bodyMultiple * average(high[1..lookback] - low[1..lookback])
book_order_type: n/a (context/entry trigger, may be entered on the close of this bar -> close-and-next-open)

complexity.reason: single-bar body vs. window-average range

notes: This is the same core mechanic as Chapter 5's SharpCountertrendBreaksBreakoutPullback (point C in Figure 5.8), redefined here for the Failed Breakouts template.

name: FailedBreakoutTemplate
quote: Most breakouts fail... In terms of actual execution, the breakout failure is nothing more than a failed pullback.
description: The book's named Failed Breakouts template: setup (weak-momentum breakout, G06-56) + trigger (strong countertrend first reaction, G06-57) + stop (beyond the pullback thrust extreme, G06-58) + target (aggressive initial-risk partial profit, G06-59). May also resolve via a plain failure test at the prior high/low (G06-01), per the book's Goldman Sachs example.
pseudocode: G06-56 (weak breakout) AND G06-57 (strong countertrend reaction), OR G06-01 applied at the pullback's own extreme; managed by G06-58/G06-59
book_order_type: market/stop entry on the close of the reaction bar -> close-and-next-open

complexity.reason: aggregates simple/moderate primitives; less pivot-dependent than the other named templates

notes: Trade type: support/resistance holding. The book calls this 'the most complex and least well defined of the major trade setups' despite its comparatively simple mechanics, because judging trigger timing in real time is hard.

name: OpeningRangeDefinition
quote: A term used to describe the range price trades within a specific time following the open. Traders may use opening ranges from a few minutes to an hour.
description: Defines the opening range as the highest high and lowest low of the first N bars (or minutes) of the session, used as a breakout reference level.
pseudocode: orHigh = highest(high, orBars) over the first orBars bars of the session; orLow = lowest(low, orBars) over the same window; close[0] > orHigh
book_order_type: n/a (structural primitive); breakout mechanized as close-then-next-open

complexity.reason: a highest/lowest window anchored to the session's first N bars

notes: Grimes gives no fixed orBars; 'a few minutes to an hour' is left as a tunable parameter.

name: RangeExpansionVolatilityBreakout
quote: A market undergoing a range expansion phase will probably trend in one direction, the range of bars will probably expand, and measures of volatility will increase on some time frames.
description: Flags when the current bar's range is expanding well beyond the recent average bar range, a precursor/signal of a directional move.
pseudocode: high[0] - low[0] > expansionMult * average(high - low, lookback)

complexity.reason: a single bar's range compared to a rolling average range
